description: Implement solution.py so that it reads integers from standard input and prints the required second-largest value according to the problem specification. The input contains at least two distinct integers. The implementation must work correctly for arbitrary valid integer inputs.

files.solution.py:
import sys

numbers = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
print(sorted(numbers)[-2])
files.reference.py:
import sys

print(unique_numbers[-2])

description: Implement solution.py so that it reads integers from standard input and prints the maximum value that occurs exactly once. The input is guaranteed to contain at least one such value. The implementation must work correctly for arbitrary valid integer inputs.

files.solution.py:
import sys
from collections import Counter

numbers = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
counts = Counter(numbers)
print(max(numbers))
files.reference.py:
import sys
from collections import Counter

numbers = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
counts = Counter(numbers)
unique_values = [x for x in numbers if counts[x] == 1]
print(max(unique_values))
files.generator.py:
import random
import sys

seed = int(sys.stdin.read().strip() or 0)
random.seed(seed)

unique_values = random.sample(range(-100, 101), 3)
repeated_value = random.choice(unique_values)

values = unique_values + [repeated_value, repeated_value]
random.shuffle(values)

print(*values)
